no arguments
    quote takes FILE START END, and got 0 arguments; run "hunk quote --help"
one argument
    quote takes FILE START END, and got 1 argument; run "hunk quote --help"
two arguments
    quote takes FILE START END, and got 2 arguments; run "hunk quote --help"
four arguments
    quote takes FILE START END, and got 4 arguments; run "hunk quote --help"
START is not a number
    START and END are line numbers counted from 1, and "x" is not one
END is not a number
    START and END are line numbers counted from 1, and "2a" is not one
START is 0
    START and END are line numbers counted from 1, and "0" is not one
a sign
    START and END are line numbers counted from 1, and "+1" is not one
a fraction
    START and END are line numbers counted from 1, and "2.5" is not one
an empty number
    START and END are line numbers counted from 1, and "" is not one
a number no int holds
    START and END are line numbers counted from 1, and "99999999999999999999" is not one
a number with a control character in it
    START and END are line numbers counted from 1, and "1\x1b[2J" is not one
START after END
    START is 6 and END is 3, so the range runs backwards
a path a directive line would trim
    "f.txt " begins or ends with a space or a tab, which a directive line drops, so no patch can name it
a path with a leading tab
    "\tf.txt" begins or ends with a space or a tab, which a directive line drops, so no patch can name it
an unknown flag
    flag provided but not defined: -nwe; run "hunk quote --help"
a negative number is read as a flag
    flag provided but not defined: -3; run "hunk quote --help"
a flag with an escape in its name
    flag provided but not defined: -x<U+001B>[2J; run "hunk quote --help"
an empty --marker
    --marker must not be empty
a --marker with a newline in it
    --marker contains U+000A, a control character, and a directive line could not start with it
a FILE that is not there
    absent.txt: no such file; only @@ create makes one; the root is /the/root
a FILE that is a directory
    sub: it is a directory, not a file; the root is /the/root
a FILE outside the root
    ../out.txt: the path climbs out of the root; the root is /the/root
a FILE inside .git
    .git/config: it is .git or inside it, which is git's own and not the working tree; hunk never edits there; the root is /the/root
a FILE inside a file
    f.txt/x: no such file; f.txt is a file, so nothing can be inside it; the root is /the/root
a FILE with a control character in its name
    f<U+001B>.txt: the path contains U+001B, a control character, which hunk does not allow in a file name; remove it from the patch; the root is /the/root
an empty FILE
    FILE is empty
END past the last line
    f.txt has 10 lines, so there is no line 40
one empty line
    gap.txt line 2 is empty, and an old of nothing matches at every position in the file; quote it together with a line beside it
a directive in the range
    doc.md line 2 is "@@ old", which a patch reads as a directive and not as text; pass --marker with a prefix that no line quoted starts with, here and to the hunk that applies the patch
